title: Lucid token contrast night asset sweep
creator: Mira Patel
description: Comprehensive accessibility and visual sweep of onboarding/quickstart assets specifically for the dark theme. Deliverables include updated iconography with accessible weight, tokenized color maps for night theme, screenshot templates for docs, and a handoff package for engineering and docs teams. Goal: ensure all onboarding screens meet AA contrast for body/labels and 4.5:1 for actionable text, with clear symbol language for novice users.
acceptance_criteria: All onboarding hero and step illustrations have contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for primary labels and >= 3:1 for supportive UI text where applicable
Icon set for quickstart is available in 3 sizes (16/24/48) with on-theme variants and exported as SVG and optimized PNGs
Design tokens for night-theme color scale (primary, surface, emphasis, disabled) are published to the token registry and documented with WCAG ratios
Screenshot templates updated; two device widths (desktop 1280px, mobile 375px) with overlay masks for copy and CTA placement
Engineering handoff includes a single branch PR with sprite/svg exports and usage notes; docs team receives annotated screenshots and copy updates
design_notes: Primary approach: token-first. Create a discrete night theme palette rather than rely on color inversion to avoid hue shifts on brand accents.
Iconography: increase stroke weight for 16px icons by 10% on night theme, add simplified geometric masks to improve silhouette contrast against textured surfaces.
Screenshots: apply a subtle vignette when placing UI overlays to ensure CTA buttons remain visually prominent without changing copy placement.
Accessibility trade-offs: decided to keep some decorative illustrative gradients at lower contrast levels when they do not interfere with actionable UI, documented exceptions in the token registry.
Fallbacks: provide high-contrast icon set and label variants for users who enable high-contrast OS settings; engineering to expose `prefers-contrast` hook in CSS tokens.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff: reviewed PM goals with Jonah (PM). Agreed scope: hero screens, step illustrations, icon set, screenshot templates. Jonah requested medium priority for docs delivery.
2026-03-02 - Early explorations: produced 3 night palette options; team preferred #2 (muted indigo) for better brand legibility. Shared Figma prototype with accessibility audit traces.
2026-03-05 - Design review with Engineering: discussed export formats and sprite approach. Engineering prefers individual SVGs plus a small PNG fallback set for legacy docs renderer.
2026-03-08 - Accessibility review: ran Axe & Lighthouse against prototype screenshots. Found two CTA states below 4.5:1 on low-brightness surfaces; adjusted token luminance +12%.
2026-03-10 - PM feedback: request to produce annotated screenshots for three onboarding flows and add guidance for localizing icons where text overlays exist.
2026-03-12 - Docs sync: received note from docs lead (Hana Torres) requesting a mobile-first screenshot set and an extra narrow layout for embedded widgets.
2026-03-14 - Current: assets in Figma marked for export, token JSON draft pushed to token-registry branch. Next: finalize PR and tag engineering for handoff review.
implementation_steps: Finalize night-theme token palette and export JSON to token-registry
Produce final icon exports (SVG + 1x/2x PNG) and upload to design-assets repo
Update screenshot templates and generate annotated variants for desktop/mobile/narrow
Open handoff PR with usage notes, contrast rationale, and exceptions list
Coordinate with docs to replace screenshots in onboarding quickstart and attach annotated assets
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: localized copy may overlap icons in some languages -> Mitigation: provide spacing rules and alternate icon placements in the guidance doc
Risk: legacy docs renderer strips SVG masks -> Mitigation: include optimized PNG fallbacks and test on docs staging
Risk: contrast changes conflict with brand color -> Mitigation: documented brand-safe token aliases and secured sign-off from Brand team before release
